name: Against Heresies
author: Irenaeus

sourceObservations.observation: Irenaeus describes several positions that distinguish Jesus, Christ, and the Saviour, then states that he will compare those positions with the overall witness of the apostles.
sourceObservations.evidenceNote: This records the argumentative setup of the reviewed section without adopting Irenaeus's characterization or conclusion.

sourceObservations.observation: Irenaeus appeals to John and Matthew, including Matthew's birth and naming account, to argue that Jesus and Christ are one and the same rather than separate figures.
sourceObservations.evidenceNote: This records Irenaeus's use of the cited apostolic writings within the reviewed section; it is not a Divine Core doctrinal assessment.

sourceObservations.observation: Irenaeus continues the same argument through writings of Paul and Mark, relating the one Jesus Christ to Davidic descent, birth from Mary, divine sonship, resurrection, and humanity’s reception of adoption through him.
sourceObservations.evidenceNote: This neutrally summarizes the sequence of claims and texts used in the reviewed section without evaluating their doctrinal validity.

divineCoreAssessment.authorityBoundary: This assessment is provisional and revisable reasoning under the Divine Core Constitution. It is not final doctrine, automatic acceptance, human or ecclesial approval, or an independent source of theological authority.

scripturalDoctrinalEvaluation.governingPrinciple: Scripture is the governing written authority. Patristic and other theological sources are subordinate witnesses whose claims must be tested by Scripture and accountable Christian doctrine.

The scoped text was also checked against the New Advent transcription identifying the Roberts and Rambaut translation and the 1885 Ante-Nicene Fathers publication; that transcription states that it was subsequently revised and edited for New Advent.
